chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Murram from his father from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the crescent girds itself (is visible), it is for two nights, and when you see the shadow of your head in it, it is for three." These two reports, and whatever runs in their manner and is in their meaning, are only a sign for the consideration of the entry of the month if there is an impediment in the sky from clouds and what runs in its manner. Then it is permissible at that time to consider it in the coming night by the girding of the crescent and its hiding before or after the twilight. As for when the impediment is removed and the sky is clear, these things are not considered, and that runs in the manner of the testimony of two witnesses from outside the town. Their testimony is only considered if there is an impediment there, and when there is no impediment there, it is not permissible to consider that in any way, but it requires the testimony of fifty people as we have mentioned before. And when we use these reports in some situations, our duty is cleared and we are not rejecting them, and as for what was narrated:

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: Twilight (redness in the sky after sunset)
key_terms.تَطَوُّقُ الْهِلَالِ: The crescent moon girding itself (becoming visible as a thin sliver)
key_terms.ظِلُّ الرَّأْسِ: The shadow of the head (indicating the moon is higher and more visible)

ai.seo_question: How is the start of Ramadan determined by crescent visibility versus witness testimony in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the jurisprudential hierarchy between astronomical calculation (*hisab*) and witness testimony (*shahada*) for sighting the crescent. It establishes that visual signs like the crescent's girth or shadow are merely evidentiary markers valid only when an impediment like clouds obscures the sky, whereas clear skies require the standard testimony of fifty witnesses, mirroring the principle of distant witness validity.
